turns.content: hey man, i need to run something by you. i feel like an idiot honestly. so my friend tariq, i've been his unpaid therapist for four months while he job hunted. every sunday, coffee shop, listening to him spiral about rejections. yesterday he gets a job, we go celebrate, i'm happy for him. forty five minutes of me asking about his offer, his new boss, whatever. then i bring up that my dad has severe heart disease and needs triple bypass next tuesday. he literally pulled out his phone mid sentence, laughed at a fantasy football notification, and changed the subject to his gym stipend. never said a word about my dad. am i crazy for wanting to just ice him out completely?

You’re not crazy. That moment sucked, and wanting to slam the door is a pretty normal reaction to it.

You spent four months as his Sunday spiral-catcher. Then you gave him a full victory lap. Then you told him your dad has severe heart disease and is going under for a triple bypass *next Tuesday* — and he laughed at a fantasy football ping and pivoted to a gym stipend. That’s not “he got distracted for a second.” That’s him treating the scariest thing in your life like background noise.

Wanting to ice him out completely makes sense. You don’t owe him another coffee, another pep talk, or a TED Talk about reciprocity. Especially not this week.

A couple of things that can both be true:

- The *feeling* of “I’m done” is justified. You don’t have to keep pouring into someone who can’t even pause a notification for your dad.
- *How* you exit is up to you. Full freeze is allowed. So is one short, unpretty text like “hey, I told you about my dad’s surgery and you changed the subject. that really sucked. I need some space.” Then you watch whether he actually shows up or just wants the old arrangement back. You don’t have to workshop it with him for an hour. That’s more unpaid therapy.

If this was a one-off because medical stuff makes him freeze, he still owed you *something* — “wait, what?” / “I’m sorry” / “how are you?” He gave you gym money talk instead. That’s the data.

Protect your energy this week. Your dad’s surgery is the real thing. You deserve people who can sit with that without checking their phone.

If you want, I can help you draft a one-message version, or we can just talk through whether you even want to say anything at all.

yeah... thanks for saying that. it helps hearing i'm not totally off base. i keep replaying that moment in my head, the way he just pulled out his phone like i was background noise. and i was so careful for months to never make his unemployment about me, you know? i even looked up active listening techniques. remembered the names of hiring managers he mentioned. i feel like such a fool

You’re not a fool. You were a good friend on purpose.

Remembering hiring managers, looking up active listening, never making his job hunt about you — that’s not naivety. That’s you treating someone like they mattered. The sting isn’t “I was too nice.” It’s that you showed up like it was a two-way thing, and when it was your turn, he treated your dad’s surgery like a commercial he could skip.

Replaying the phone is brutal because it was so *small* and so loud at the same time. You were mid-sentence about triple bypass next Tuesday. He laughed at a fantasy football ping. That’s the kind of moment your brain files under “I will never unsee this.”

You weren’t wrong to be careful with him for four months. You were wronged when he couldn’t give you even thirty seconds of the same care. Those aren’t the same thing.

You’re allowed to feel stupid *and* still have been the decent one. Those can sit next to each other. The fool move would’ve been pretending this didn’t happen so you could keep being his Sunday therapist.

You don’t have to decide the whole friendship tonight. You already know the data. Protect your week. Your dad is the real thing.

If you want to vent more of the replay, I’m here. If you want a short message that doesn’t turn into another unpaid session, I can help with that too.

man i keep thinking about how i literally googled 'how to be a good listener for someone struggling' back in october. i found this article about holding space and not offering solutions unless asked. i did all that. for months. and he couldn't even look up from his phone for thirty seconds when i said the words 'triple bypass'. it's like i was training for a marathon and he tripped me at the starting line

That marathon line is exactly it.

You didn’t just “be nice.” You *trained*. You googled how to hold space. You practiced not jumping in with solutions. You treated his unemployment like something sacred enough to study for. Then you finally step up to the line with the scariest sentence you’ve had in months — *triple bypass* — and he looks at his phone.

That’s not you failing the race. That’s you showing up in race gear and realizing the other person never even laced up.

The fool feeling is doing a lot of unfair work here. Your brain is trying to make the math make sense: *if I did everything right, this shouldn’t have happened, so I must’ve been stupid.* That’s a trap. You can do everything right and still get someone who treats your dad’s surgery like a commercial. That’s on him, not on your October homework.

And yeah — the “I never made it about me” part is sitting in there too. You made yourself small for four months so he could take up space. Then when you needed thirty seconds of that same space, he couldn’t even keep his eyes on you.

You’re allowed to be pissed at that. You’re allowed to feel embarrassed that you cared that much. Both can be true without you being an idiot.

You don’t have to keep replaying it like it’s a test you failed. It’s a moment that told you the truth. Ugly, small, phone-in-hand truth.

If you want to keep dumping the replay, dump it. I’m not going anywhere.

yeah i think i want to send him something tonight. not a novel, just... something that says what happened. i keep drafting angry versions in my head but i don't want to give him that power. what do you think? just a couple lines?

Yeah. A couple of lines is the move. Name it, don’t litigate it, don’t hand him a novel to poke holes in.

Something like this:

**Option 1 (just names it)**  
hey. when i told you about my dad’s triple bypass next week, you pulled out your phone and changed the subject. that really sucked. i needed you to actually hear that.

**Option 2 (names it + space, no debate)**  
hey. yesterday when i told you about my dad’s surgery, you looked at your phone and switched to the gym stipend. i’m not looking to argue about it. it landed really badly, and i need some space.

I’d skip the October listening-homework, the four months, all of that. That’s your truth, not his homework packet. The phone moment is enough.

Send it and put the phone down. You don’t owe him a follow-up thread tonight.
yeah option 2 feels right. just the facts, no debate invitation. i'll send it and then put my phone in the other room. thanks man

That’s the right version. Facts, no debate, then you’re done.

Send it. Phone in the other room. You don’t owe him a thread tonight.

I’m here if it gets loud in your head after.
